historical_anchor: US submarines historically sighted/attacked major Japanese cruiser groups moving between Davao and Lingga on 6-7 Apr; Branch uses this only as a sanity anchor for submarine observation opportunity, not as an automatic exact ship encounter.

branch_result.US_information: One or more intermittent submarine reports confirm heavy Japanese surface movement on the southern Philippines/Celebes approach routes. Confidence rises that a major fleet pool is concentrating south, but carrier count/precise anchorage remains unresolved.
branch_result.Japanese_loss: No major fleet ship loss centered in this window. Improved route ASW, routing discipline and speed reduce attack opportunities but do not eliminate submarine contact risk.
branch_result.weapon_quality_on_carriers: NO. US submarines do not deliver a fresh, complete fix on the five-carrier body.

effect: Both sides gain warning-level information without forcing battle: Japan treats submarines as a basing hazard and rotates anchorages; the US avoids assuming the Japanese carriers are absent merely because no exact carrier visual is obtained.
